trial_name.text: Study 103,004 (Tetra-HD), a 12-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-center study of tetrabenazine for Huntington's chorea

citations.quote: Study 103,004 - A 12 week randomized, double-blind, placebo controlled, multi-center study of tetrabenazine for the treatment of Huntington's chorea (Tetra HD)
Study 103,004 - A 12 week randomized, double-blind, placebo controlled, multi-center study of tetrabenazine for the treatment of Huntington's chorea (Tetra HD)

phase.text: Not stated; a 12-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled multi-center acute treatment study

citations.quote: In one study, a 12 week study of tetrabenazine for the acute treatment of chorea in patients with Huntington's disease, the primary endpoint data support the proposed indication (p<0.0001).

design.text: Multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study with two parallel unbalanced (2:1) groups, titrated to best dose up to 100 mg/day over 12 weeks

citations.quote: This was a multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, study of the efficacy, tolerability, and safety of tetrabenazine (titrated to best dose) in two parallel unbalanced (2:1) groups of participants suffering from manifest Huntington's disease.

population.text: Ambulatory patients with manifest Huntington's disease (chorea, positive family history, genetic confirmation), with a Total Maximal Chorea Score >= 10 at baseline

citations.quote: The efficacy of XENAZINE as a treatment for the chorea of Huntington's disease was established primarily in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled multi-center trial (Study 1) conducted in ambulatory patients with a diagnosis of Huntington's disease (HD).
In this study, participants were required to have a Total Maximal Chorea Score \ge 10 at baseline.

endpoint.text: Change from baseline in UHDRS item 12 (Total/Maximal Chorea Score), the difference between baseline and the average of the week 9 and week 12 scores

citations.quote: The 12 week acute treatment study, TBZ 103,004, was positive on the primary endpoint, the difference between the baseline and the average of the week 9 and week 12 scores on Unified Huntington's Disease Rating Scale (UHDRS) item 12 (maximal chorea), p=0.0001.
Figure 1. Mean \pm s.e.m. Changes from Baseline in Total Chorea Score in 84 HD Subjects Treated with Tetrabenazine (n = 54) or Placebo (n = 30)

result.text: Total Chorea Score declined by a mean 5.0 units on tetrabenazine vs 1.5 units on placebo; treatment effect 3.5 units (p<0.0001)

citations.quote: As seen in Table 3, chorea scores for participants in the tetrabenazine group declined from baseline to the maintenance period by a mean of 5.0 units, while those in the placebo group declined by 1.5 units. The treatment effect of 3.5 units is highly significant (p<0.0001).

indication.text: XENAZINE is indicated for the treatment of chorea associated with Huntington's disease.

citations.quote: XENAZINE is indicated for the treatment of chorea associated with Huntington's disease.

target_moa.text: Tetrabenazine is a reversible depletor of monoamines (dopamine, serotonin, norepinephrine, histamine) from nerve terminals; it reversibly inhibits the human vesicular monoamine transporter type 2 (VMAT2) (Ki ~100 nM), decreasing uptake of monoamines into synaptic vesicles and depleting monoamine stores.

citations.quote: The precise mechanism by which tetrabenzazine exerts its anti-chorea effects is unknown, but is believed to be related to its effect as a reversible depletor of monoamines (such as dopamine, serotonin, norepinephrine, and histamine) from nerve terminals.

Tetrabenzazine reversibly inhibits the human vesicular monoamine transporter type 2 (VMAT2) (K_i \approx 100 nM), resulting in decreased uptake of monoamines into synaptic vesicles and depletion of monoamine stores.

modality.text: Small molecule (selective centrally acting monoamine depletor / VMAT2 inhibitor)

citations.quote: Tetrabenazine, a selective centrally acting monoamine depletor, was initially developed by Hoffmann-La Roche in the mid-1950s as an antipsychotic drug.

key_safety.text: Most common AEs (>10%, >=5% over placebo) were sedation/somnolence (31% vs 3%), fatigue (22% vs 13%), insomnia (22% vs 0%), depression (19% vs 0%), akathisia (19% vs 0%), and nausea (13% vs 7%). Depression/suicidality is the key serious risk; 10 of 54 (19%) tetrabenazine patients had an AE of depression or worsening depression vs none of 30 placebo.

citations.quote: The AEs most commonly reported (over 10%, and at least 5% greater than placebo) were sedation/somnolence (31% vs. 3% on placebo), fatigue (22% vs. 13% on placebo), insomnia (22% vs. 0% on placebo), depression (19% vs. 0% on placebo), akathisia (19% vs. 0% on placebo), and nausea (13% vs. 7% on placebo).

In a 12-week, double-blind placebo-controlled study in patients with chorea associated with Huntington's disease, 10 of 54 patients (19%) treated with tetrabenazine were reported to have an adverse event of depression or worsening depression compared to none of the 30 placebo-treated patients.

detail.text: XENAZINE can increase the risk of depression and suicidal thoughts and behavior (suicidality) in patients with Huntington's disease; it is contraindicated in patients who are actively suicidal and in those with untreated or inadequately treated depression.

citations.quote: XENAZINE can increase the risk of depression and suicidal thoughts and behavior (suicidality) in patients with Huntington's disease. Anyone considering the use of XENAZINE must balance the risks of depression and suicidality with the clinical need for control of choreiform movements. Close observation of patients for the emergence or worsening of depression, suicidality, or unusual changes in beha

XENAZINE is contraindicated in patients who are actively suicidal, and in patients with untreated or inadequately treated depression. (see CONTRAINDICATIONS; WARNINGS - Increased Risk of Depression and Suicidality, and PRECAUTIONS - Information for Patients).

detail.text: A REMS was required to ensure the benefits outweigh the risks of depression and suicidality; it consists of a Medication Guide, communication plan, a timetable for assessments, and assessments of the REMS.

citations.quote: In accordance with 505-1 of the FDCA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for Xenazine (tetrabenazine) Tablets, 12.5 and 25 mg, to ensure that the benefits of the drug outweigh the risks of depression and suicidality.
The REMS consists of a Medication Guide, communication plan, a timetable for assessments, and assessments of the REMS.

detail.text: No companion diagnostic required; however, CYP2D6 genotyping is required before giving doses above 50 mg/day.

citations.quote: Doses above 50 mg should not be given without CYP2D6 genotyping (see WARNINGS: Laboratory Tests and PRECAUTIONS—Drug Interactions).

vote.text: The Peripheral and Central Nervous Systems Drugs Advisory Committee met on 12/6/07 and voted overwhelmingly to recommend approval of the application.

citations.quote: In addition, this application was discussed at a meeting of the Peripheral and Central Nervous Systems Drugs Advisory Committee (PCNS AC) on 12/6/07.
Despite these concerns, the AC voted overwhelmingly to recommend approval of the application.

detail.text: Not approved first cycle; the Agency issued three previous Approvable letters (on 3/24/06, 12/26/07, and 3/18/08). The sponsor's June 16, 2008 submission constituted a complete response to the March 18, 2008 action letter, which led to approval.

citations.quote: The Agency has issued three previous Approvable letters: on 3/24/06, 12/26/07, and 3/18/08.
The June 16, 2008, submission constituted a complete response to our March 18, 2008, action letter.

Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) dated September 23, 2005, received September 23, 2005, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act for Xenzazine® (tetrabenazine) Tablets 12.5 and 25 mg.

requirement.text: Complete the ongoing 2-year carcinogenicity study in male rats to identify the unexpected serious risk of carcinogenicity (Final Report by March 2009).

citations.quote: Complete the ongoing 2-year carcinogenicity study in male rats to identify the unexpected serious risk of carcinogenicity.

requirement.text: Conduct a 2-year carcinogenicity study in female rats to identify the unexpected serious risk of carcinogenicity (Final Report by January 2013).

citations.quote: Conduct a 2-year carcinogenicity study in female rats to identify the unexpected serious risk of carcinogenicity.

requirement.text: Conduct a nonclinical toxicity study of fertility and early embryonic development (to implantation) to identify the unexpected serious risk of adverse effects on reproduction.

citations.quote: Conduct a nonclinical toxicity study of fertility and early embryonic development (to implantation) to identify the unexpected serious risk of adverse effects on reproduction.

requirement.text: Submit in vivo metabolism data in the animal species used in the nonclinical (reproductive toxicology and carcinogenicity) studies of tetrabenazine.

citations.quote: Submit *in vivo* metabolism data in the animal species used in the nonclinical studies of tetrabenazine, particularly the reproductive toxicology and the carcinogenicity studies.

requirement.text: Conduct a neurotoxicity study of tetrabenazine using methodology and a multiple dose regimen similar to Satou et al. (2001).

citations.quote: Conduct a neurotoxicity study of tetrabenazine using methodology and a multiple dose regimen similar to Satou T et al. *Exp Toxicol Pathol* 53(4):303-308, 2001.

requirement.text: Conduct an in vitro metabolism study to characterize the inhibitory effect of tetrabenazine, alpha-HTBZ, and beta-HTBZ on CYP2B6.

citations.quote: Conduct an *in vitro* metabolism study to characterize the potential serious safety risk of the inhibitory effect of tetrabenazine, \alpha-HTBZ, and \beta-HTBZ on CYP2B6.

orphan_indication.text: Tetrabenazine (Xenazine) for the chorea of Huntington's disease has an orphan drug designation.

citations.quote: Because this drug for this indication has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.

summary.text: Xenazine (tetrabenazine) was approved for the chorea of Huntington's disease, an orphan-designated indication, after review that included a PCNS Advisory Committee meeting (12/6/07) and three prior Approvable letters; approval was conditioned on a REMS to address depression/suicidality risk and required postmarketing nonclinical studies.

citations.quote: Because this drug for this indication has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.
In addition, this application was discussed at a meeting of the Peripheral and Central Nervous Systems Drugs Advisory Committee (PCNS AC) on 12/6/07.

In accordance with 505-1 of the FDCA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for Xenazine (tetrabenazine) Tablets, 12.5 and 25 mg, to ensure that the benefits of the drug outweigh the risks of depression and suicidality.
